_comment: forest_bars: Map 3's start/finish gate, the forest's answer to rock_bars. A fallen-log sill across the ground, two thick living end posts grown out of it, a lintel log across their tops, 20 BRANCH bars socketed into the sill's top quads and the lintel's underside quads, two lashing rails welded into the posts at mid height, four leaf sprays where the frame is living wood. A bar is a branch, not a bar: an irregular taper that loses most of its girth in its first third, a bow through the thickness, its own wander and one or two kinks across the lane, a swelling at each knot, short cut stubs where side branches were taken off, and on every fourth bar a fork near the top whose second limb is welded into the lintel's front face. The lintel's lane boundaries drift across the gate, so no two bars stand at the same angle. 10.6 x 8.5 m filling the lane's cross-section, 0.79 m thick; no opening wider than 0.335 m anywhere, at any height, in any direction (limit 0.38). Origin at the base centre, y=0 is the ground; the gate spans local X, thickness along local Z. One textured material (the forest 256x256 atlas + emissive), one UV set, one contiguous mesh (components=1, duplicate seam vertices=0), no skin, no animation. ForestBarsCollision is the sill, the lintel, the two posts, one box per bar spanning that bar's widest reach (fork included, clamped to the gate's own thickness) and one per rail, shipped as a `-colonly` node; Godot turns it into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `surfaces` stays 1 and `max_tris` counts only what is drawn.
